subject: Order Form ST-422 — end-of-term coordination & fallback cadence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ST-422 — recommended redlines for term/renewal sections (draft)

Team —

Attached are my suggested edits for the Order Form and the small playbook I think Sales/CS should have ready if StratoTech asks about exit mechanics. High-level notes: 

- Auto-renew: propose default 45-day notice for pilot/SMB; customer asked previously for 60 days for Enterprise. Suggest we surface a tiered notice window in the Order Form so we can be flexible without re-negotiating the MSA.
- Termination for convenience: redline keeps the right but adds a 30-day service wind-down and pro-rated credits for prepaid periods. Avoids long litigation risk while protecting committed capacity.
- Billing stop effective date: clarify it as the end of the termination window (not receipt of notice) to avoid pro-rated disputes.
- Transition support: 30-day paid transition for Enterprise with optional discounted data export job.

I've attached an annotated PDF plus a short spreadsheet that maps notice windows to refund/credit outcomes. If Aditya wants to start with a softer ask to the customer, we can soften the TFoC language and push the operational playbook instead.

Attachments: [Attachment: SF_OrderForm_ST-422_redline.pdf (PDF, 32KB)], [Attachment: end_of_term_playbook.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@stratotech.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form ST-422 — proposed term & notice approach (please review)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, attaching a clean copy and a redline focused only on the Term / Renewal / Termination sections so legal can move quickly. The two main adjustments we propose:

1) Tiered auto-renew notice windows — 45 days for Pilot & Growth tiers, 60 days for Enterprise. This matches how customers consume capacity and lets us lower friction for short pilots.
2) Termination for convenience — allow either party to terminate with a 30-day wind-down; for Enterprise customers we propose a 30-day transition service and pro-rated credits for pre-paid months.

Action items for StratoTech: please confirm whether you need a flat 60-day notice for all tiers or if tiering is acceptable. If you prefer a flat 60-day approach, we can accept that for Enterprise but would like to retain 45 days for pilots to avoid over-committing capacity. 

If acceptable, our Legal team will incorporate the agreed language into a final Order Form for e-signature.

Attachments: [Attachment: SF_OrderForm_ST-422_redline.pdf], [Attachment: end_of_term_playbook.xlsx]

Best,

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form ST-422 — proposed term & notice approach (please review)

Aditya —

Thank you for the redline. A few immediate items from our side: 

- Our procurement/legal team prefers a single uniform 60-day notice window across all tiers for operational predictability. Shorter windows create churn risk for our procurement planning.
- The proposed 30-day wind-down under TFoC is concerning. Our finance team wants clarity that any billing stop aligns with the effective termination date and that we are not billed for unconsumed committed units after the effective date. If you keep a 30-day wind-down, we would expect pro-rated credits to be automatic (no additional claims process).
- We need the transition support to be explicitly scoped (what constitutes 'data export job' and who bears the cost).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a flat 60-day notice and the following changes: automatic pro-rated credits at termination effective date; explicit scope for the 30-day transition (one export job included for Enterprise)?

We'd like to get to a final Order Form by next Thursday (6/3) if possible.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Procurement Operations
StratoTech

Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form ST-422 — proposed term & notice approach (please review)

Elena —

Thanks — very helpful notes. Quick response and a concrete compromise that should keep procurement happy while protecting Redwood's capacity economics: 

1) Notice window: agree to a flat 60-day notice for all Enterprise-specified subscriptions. For Pilot/Proof-of-Value engagements we will document a 45-day notice in an Order Form addendum; that addendum will be a documented exception rather than the default MSA term. This keeps your operational predictability for Enterprise while giving pilots flexibility.

2) Billing stop & credits: we will make pro-rated credits automatic and calculate them from the effective termination date (end of the notice window). No manual claim process. We will add the formula in the Order Form so it's auditable.

3) Transition support scope: for Enterprise customers we will provide one complimentary data export (up to 100GB) and up to two support engineering hours for orchestration. Any additional export work can be quoted separately. We'll add that language to the Order Form.

If that aligns with StratoTech, I'll ask Legal to issue a final clean Order Form for signature today.
